title: ACIM-QMM: Efficient Analog Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for QC-MDPC McEliece Cryptosystem
problem: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementations like QC-MDPC McEliece suffer from high latency and large hardware overhead in digital computing paradigm.
motivation: Quantum computing threat to current encryption necessitates PQC deployment; QMM requires key generation and encryption operations with high performance demands.
method: The system uses analog circuits (circuits that work with continuous electrical signals rather than discrete 1s and 0s) paired with computing-in-memory technology (performing calculations directly in storage rather than moving data between processor and memory) to execute the matrix operations needed for QMM key generation and encryption. This avoids the digital computing bottleneck where traditional processors repeatedly copy data between CPU and memory. The catch is that analog circuits produce small measurement errors, but the system keeps these errors small enough to preserve cryptographic correctness.
key_novelty: This is the first use of analog computing-in-memory (math done directly in storage with continuous electrical signals) to replace the digital multiplication-accumulation steps (repeated multiply-and-add operations) in post-quantum cryptography.
contributions: Analog CIM architecture for QC-MDPC McEliece cryptosystem
31.4x to 288.1x speedup compared to SOTA QMM hardware
3.12x area efficiency and 20.32x energy efficiency vs other PQC hardware
Low-error analog computation for cryptographic primitives
primary_theme: analog CIM for post-quantum cryptography acceleration
